summary: Onboarding batch for @cipherstash/cli plus one change to @cipherstash/stack's Drizzle column type. The release risk is concentrated in a new migration rewriter: any drizzle-kit `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE eql_v2_encrypted` is replaced by ADD tmp column, a *commented-out* UPDATE, DROP original column, RENAME. Because the backfill is a comment and the temp column only exists once the migration runs, applying the rewritten migration to a populated table irreversibly deletes the original column's data and leaves the encrypted column NULL. Previously such migrations failed loudly with a cast error. The wizard (which encrypts columns it introspects from an existing database) now runs this rewrite and then offers `drizzle-kit migrate` with default 'yes'; `db install` auto-detects Drizzle and sweeps every .sql file in the migrations folder without prompting. The Drizzle `dataType()` string also changed for all existing @cipherstash/stack users, which may make drizzle-kit regenerate ALTERs for already-encrypted columns that the sweep would then turn into DROPs. Lesser risks: `db setup` was removed while bundled skills (now copied into customer repos) and the stack README still instruct it; Drizzle auto-detection silently changes `db install` from a direct install to migration generation. The new rewriter tests pass in CI but assert the destructive output rather than guard against it. Advisory verdict: changes or verification required.

behaviour_changes.description: New rewriteEncryptedAlterColumns() rewrites every matching `ALTER TABLE .. ALTER COLUMN .. SET DATA TYPE eql_v2_encrypted ...;` statement in every .sql file of the Drizzle out dir into ADD tmp column / commented-out UPDATE / DROP original column / RENAME. Files are overwritten in place.

The wizard's post-agent step now runs `drizzle-kit generate`, applies the rewrite to the first existing of drizzle/, migrations/, src/db/migrations/, then prompts to run `drizzle-kit migrate` (default yes). `db install` on the Drizzle path runs the same sweep (skipping only the install-eql file) with no prompt.

@cipherstash/stack `encryptedType` Drizzle custom type now returns '"public"."eql_v2_encrypted"' from dataType() instead of 'eql_v2_encrypted'; getEncryptedColumnConfig accepts both forms. This is what drizzle-kit records in schema snapshots and emits into generated SQL.
`stash db setup` removed (now falls through to 'Unknown db subcommand'); `db install` scaffolds stash.config.ts when missing.

`db install` auto-detects Drizzle (drizzle.config.* or drizzle-orm/drizzle-kit in package.json) and Supabase (DATABASE_URL host). When Drizzle is detected it generates a migration file instead of installing EQL into the database. On the direct path, a non-superuser role without explicit flags is switched to the no-operator-family variant and the missing-permissions abort is skipped.

CLI build copies the monorepo `skills/` into dist/skills; the wizard offers to copy stash-encryption/stash-drizzle/stash-supabase/stash-cli skills into the customer's ./.claude/skills (force overwrite).

CLI loads .env.local, .env.development.local, .env.development, then .env (first value wins) instead of only .env, so DATABASE_URL may resolve to a different database than before for projects with several env files.

Wizard writes .cipherstash/wizard-log.md, prints a report-only scan of call sites, and an experimental `env` command is registered (gated by STASH_EXPERIMENTAL_ENV_CMD per PR). Read only at diff level.

failure_scenarios.title: Rewritten migration drops the original column's data on populated tables
failure_scenarios.trigger: A user runs the wizard (or `db install` in a Drizzle project) against an existing app whose tables already have rows, choosing columns to encrypt; drizzle-kit generates `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE eql_v2_encrypted`, and the migration is applied (wizard default answer is yes).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: renderSafeAlter emits ADD COLUMN tmp, the UPDATE only as a SQL comment, then DROP COLUMN original and RENAME (rewrite-migrations.ts:67-78). Nothing copies or encrypts existing values; the guidance to 'backfill the new column BEFORE running this migration' cannot be followed because the tmp column is created by this same migration. The wizard rewrites then prompts `drizzle-kit migrate` with initialValue true (post-agent.ts:71-87), and finishes with 'Your data is now protected' (run.ts:226). Previously the same migration failed with a cast error, leaving data intact.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Irreversible loss of the original column contents (only recoverable from backup); the encrypted column is NULL for every existing row, so the app reads nulls. A loud, safe failure becomes a silent destructive success.

existing_verification.description: rewrite-migrations.test.ts asserts the rewritten text contains ADD/DROP/RENAME; it encodes the destructive output and does not check data preservation.

missing_verification: An integration test applying the rewritten migration to a table with rows and checking values are preserved or the migration refuses to run.
The PR's own manual smoke tests are unchecked.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Do not emit DROP COLUMN in the same migration as the ADD. Split into (1) ADD tmp column, (2) app-side backfill with encryptModel, (3) a separate DROP/RENAME migration; or emit a guard (e.g. DO block raising if the original column has non-null rows) before DROP. Default the wizard's migrate prompt to 'no' when rewrites occurred.

failure_scenarios.title: Sweep rewrites every existing migration file, including hand-fixed or not-yet-deployed ones
failure_scenarios.trigger: A Drizzle project (auto-detected, no flag) runs `db install` or the wizard while its migrations folder contains earlier ALTERs to eql_v2_encrypted, including ones a user hand-edited with a USING conversion, or ones committed but not yet applied in staging/production.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The regex ends in `[^;]*;`, so any trailing clause such as `USING ...` is matched and discarded (rewrite-migrations.ts:14-15). The loop overwrites every .sql file in outDir (rewrite-migrations.ts:42-62); install.ts skips only the install-eql file (install.ts:337-340) and Drizzle detection needs no flag (install.ts:172-178). Rewritten files are not reported for confirmation, just logged.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Committed migration history is silently altered; environments that have not yet applied the file run the DROP version instead of the author's data-preserving conversion, with the FS-1 data loss in those environments.

existing_verification.description: No test covers a USING clause or an already-applied migration; tests only cover bare statements.

missing_verification: Test that statements with USING clauses are left alone.
Test that only newly generated migration files are rewritten.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Restrict the rewrite to files generated in the current run (compare against the drizzle journal before/after), refuse to touch statements with USING, and ask before overwriting.

failure_scenarios.title: Changed Drizzle dataType string causes regenerated ALTERs on already-encrypted columns, which the sweep turns into DROPs
failure_scenarios.trigger: An existing @cipherstash/stack + Drizzle user upgrades, runs `drizzle-kit generate`, then runs the wizard or `db install`.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: dataType() changes from 'eql_v2_encrypted' (base drizzle/index.ts:96) to '"public"."eql_v2_encrypted"' (head :12,:104). drizzle-kit snapshots store the column type string; a different string is likely diffed as a type change, producing `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE "public"."eql_v2_encrypted"` for columns that already hold ciphertext. Alone that statement is a same-type no-op, but the rewriter matches it and emits DROP of the existing encrypted column.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Loss of stored ciphertext for existing encrypted columns (data unrecoverable without backup).

existing_verification.description: No test in packages/stack covers the dataType string or drizzle-kit snapshot behaviour after the change.

missing_verification: Run drizzle-kit generate against a snapshot created with the previous release and confirm no ALTER is emitted.
Verify what SQL drizzle-kit writes for a quoted, schema-qualified custom type name in CREATE TABLE.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Verify drizzle-kit diff behaviour before release; if it emits ALTERs, document the upgrade or make the rewriter skip ALTERs whose source column is already eql_v2_encrypted (e.g. compare against the previous snapshot).

failure_scenarios.title: Drizzle auto-detection changes `db install` from installing EQL to only writing a migration
failure_scenarios.trigger: A project with drizzle-orm in package.json (but applying EQL directly, e.g. in CI or scripts) runs `db install` without flags; or a non-superuser Neon/RDS Drizzle user.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: resolveProviderOptions enables drizzle when detectDrizzle() is true (install.ts:172-178), and installCommand then returns after generateDrizzleMigration (install.ts:55-65) without touching the database; the exit is 'Done!'. On that path excludeOperatorFamily stays false unless passed (install.ts:180, 287-290), so the non-superuser OPE fallback (install.ts:89-98) does not apply and the full-variant migration may fail at migrate time.
failure_scenarios.consequence: EQL silently not installed (subsequent `db push` or app queries fail), or a migration that fails on managed Postgres. Loud downstream, recoverable with `--drizzle=false`/flags.

failure_scenarios.mitigation: Prompt before switching to the Drizzle path when auto-detected, and apply the superuser check/OPE fallback on the Drizzle path too.
